questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes allotropy?

options.text: The existence of a substance in two or more different forms.
The ability of a substance to conduct electricity.
The process of combining two elements to form a compound.
The ability of a substance to change states.

questions.explanation: Allotropy refers to the existence of a chemical element in two or more different forms, known as allotropes, which can have different physical properties. For carbon, the well-known allotropes include diamond, graphite, and amorphous carbon.

distractorRationale.b: This describes conductivity rather than allotropy.

questions.stem: What is the main reason for the difference in properties between diamond and graphite?

options.text: The type of chemical bonds present.
The size of the carbon atoms.
The temperature at which they are formed.

distractorRationale.b: Color does not determine physical properties.
distractorRationale.c: Carbon atoms are the same size in both allotropes.
distractorRationale.d: Temperature of formation does not directly affect their properties.
